provenance.claim_boundary: Original EXP29.03 three-policy, ten-repetition comparison on nine frozen synthetic Python patches and seven declared tests. Wall time covers Python subprocess execution on a CPU, including process startup, and says nothing about production repository validation, Kimi/K3 coding quality, or other patch populations.

population.kind: nine frozen synthetic Python repository patches, including an invalid patch, a pre-existing baseline failure, and a defect outside the test universe
population.denominator: all 9 patches crossed with all 3 policies and 10 paired repetitions; invalid and baseline-failing cases retained
population.stopping_rule: Run every patch-policy-repetition once without replacement or outcome-dependent retry. A ladder stops at its first failed command or when all required predicates are covered.

repository.name: synthetic-label-normalizer
repository.default_baseline_expression: [part.strip().casefold() for part in text.split(',') if part.strip()]
repository.runtime: Python standard library; each test is a separate subprocess against a disposable patch file

independent_oracle.rule: A candidate is defective when any independent oracle case fails; a green ladder on such a candidate is false confidence. The duplicate case is never available to any policy.

patches.expression: [part.strip().casefold() for part in text.split(',') if part.strip()]
[part.strip().casefold() for part in text.split(';') if part.strip()]
[part.casefold() for part in text.split(',') if part.strip()]
[part.strip().lower() for part in text.split(',') if part.strip()]
sorted(part.strip().casefold() for part in text.split(',') if part.strip())
['a'] if text == 'a,a' else [part.strip().casefold() for part in text.split(',') if part.strip()]

fixture.question: How do broad-first, targeted-first, and coverage-and-cost adaptive validation ladders trade defect detection, predicate coverage, false confidence, commands, and measured wall time on the same patches?
